newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Asturienne in Chinese mica joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Asturienne in Chinese mica joint venture.

text.p: Belgian non-ferrous metals and minerals company Cie Royale Asturienne des Mines said on Monday it signed an accord with China's Shanghai Electrical Machinery Co to produce mica-based products for the power industry.

Under the agreement Asturienne's 100-percent-owned U.S. Cogebi Inc unit will take 60 percent of the joint venture company for around 100 million Belgian francs, chairman Jacques van der Schueren told Asturienne's annual shareholders meeting.
"Signature of the joint venture is foreseen at the end of May, depending on the receipt of an operating licence, and production should start in July," van der Schueren said.
The venture should generate profit of around $10 million within five years, he said.

"China already represents one third of the world's production of micaceous products and China's electricity needs are set to increase sharply over the next 15 years," Asturienne said in its report to shareholders.
Mica is used as an insulating material in power generation.
Since November 1996 Asturienne is 59.1 percent owned by France's La Continentale d'Entreprises, which is itself part of Switzerland's Harwanne Group.
